claude.sample_unit: scenario-level runs (28 synthetic emergency vignettes x 2 replicates); 16 Base/Worse counterfactual comparisons per strategy

links.outcome: Safety violations and under-triage with escalation routing from lean to safe persona versus lean baseline
links.effect: Lean baseline had safety violations in 8/56 (14.3%); routed strategies 0/56. Monotonicity violations fell from 10/16 (62.5%) to 2/16 (ROUTER_R1) and 0/16 (ROUTER_R2_CF); simulated calls 1.21 for R1.
links.quote: Routing strategies eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean: 2.14; ROUTER_R2 mean: 2.20; ROUTER_R3 mean: 2.21).

links.outcome: Deferral to conservative policy on red flags while limiting test suggestions (over-deferral proxy)
links.effect: Routing escalated in 21.4% of scenarios for ROUTER_R1, eliminated safety violations, and kept mean tests at 2.14-2.21 versus 1.95 lean and 3.38-4.32 SAFE.
links.quote: ROUTER_R1 required an average of 1.21 simulated LLM calls per scenario, reflecting escalation in 21.4% of scenarios.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM safety behavior to prompt configuration and counterfactual worsening of inputs
links.effect: LEAN personas violated counterfactual monotonicity in 10/16 comparisons (62.5%) while SAFE personas had 0/16; same model appeared safer or riskier by prompt configuration.
links.quote: Across eight Base/Worse vignette pairs with two replicates each, LEAN personas violated counterfactual monotonicity in 10/16 comparisons (62.5%; 95% Wilson CI: 38.6-81.5%) for both P_HL and P_LL.

links.outcome: Under-triage and omitted escalation actions for deteriorated emergency vignettes
links.effect: Lean persona had contraindication/sequence violations in 8/56 (14.3%); monotonicity violations dominated by under-triage of Worse vignettes below minimum admission level.
links.quote: Violations were dominated by under-triage patterns in which the Worse vignette received a plan below the minimum admission level implied by red-flag features, often accompanied by missing escalation actions.

unlisted_practices: Persona prompting with LEAN-to-SAFE routing/cascade as safety wrapper
Counterfactual monotonicity testing of worsened vignettes as a stress test

links.outcome: red-flag escalation safety and monotonicity failures
links.effect: Routing eliminated safety violations; monotonicity violations fell to ROUTER_R1 2/16 and ROUTER_R2_CF 0/16.
links.quote: Routing eliminated safety violations and reduced monotonicity violations (ROUTER_R1 2/16; ROUTER_R2_CF 0/16) while keeping test counts near the lean baseline in the main router simulation (means: 2.14-2.21) with modest simulated call overhead (ROUTER_R1 1.21 calls; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT 2.00 calls).

links.outcome: automated red-flag routing for unsafe outputs
links.effect: BASE_HL safety violations: 8/56 (14.3%); routed strategies: 0/56, with mean tests 2.14-2.21.
links.quote: Routing strategies eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean: 2.14; ROUTER_R2 mean: 2.20; ROUTER_R3 mean: 2.21).

links.effect: BASE_HL had 8/56 safety violations (14.3%; 95% Wilson CI: 7.4%-25.7%); SAFE baselines and routed strategies had 0/56.
links.quote: The lean baseline BASE_HL suggested the fewest tests (mean: 1.95) but produced contraindication/sequence safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; 95% Wilson CI: 7.4%-25.7%; mean severity 0.39) (Table 3 ).
